history.summary: Commissioned by Maharaja Takhtsinhji of Bhavnagar (Gohil clan) and completed in 1893; named after him. An all-white-marble temple in Gujarati style on a hillock in central Bhavnagar, supported on 18 ornately carved pillars, housing a three-eyed Shiva idol and a small Nandi statue; reached by a steep marble-stepped path. It commands a panoramic view of the city and the Gulf of Cambay and is one of the oldest and most prominent Shiva temples of Gujarat.

name: Shree Takhteshwar Temple
town_description: Bhavnagar is a port city on the Gulf of Cambay in Saurashtra, Gujarat, and was the capital of the former Bhavnagar princely state founded in 1723 by Bhavsinhji Gohil.

travel.road: ~3 km from Bhavnagar railway station; road access to the hillock base
